messageries_marseille_yokohama.summary: Messageries Impériales (renamed Messageries Maritimes 1871) extended its Far East mail line to Yokohama in 1865 (branch first via Shanghai, later direct from Hong Kong). Before the Suez Canal opened (1869) passengers/mail crossed Egypt overland (Alexandria–Suez); after 1869 the line head moved to Marseille with through-service via the canal. Industrial History of Hong Kong gives 17 April 1870 for Marseille liners running on to Yokohama fortnightly.
messageries_marseille_yokohama.ports_of_call_as_listed: Marseille – Messina/Naples – Alexandria/Port Said – Suez – Aden – Galle/Colombo – Singapore – Saigon – Hong Kong – Shanghai – Yokohama (Scamp, FEMSI vol. 2 presentation)
messageries_marseille_yokohama.missing_coords: Messina/Naples, Alexandria/Port Said, Suez, Aden, Saigon were not looked up in Wikidata (time) – add if needed.
source_sentences: Scamp: 'A branch service to Yokohama began in 1865, first via Shanghai, and then later directly from Hong Kong. When the Suez Canal was opened in 1869, the French Line ... immediately began direct service between Marseille and the Far East via that canal.'
HAL: 'La ligne principale est prolongée vers le Japon en 1865 et, après l’ouverture du canal de Suez en 1869, la tête de ligne passe de l’Égypte à Marseille.'
